The effects of different neoadjuvant regimens were compared, and pathologic characteristics were analyzed between tumor regression grade TRG1 and TRG2 groups. The χ2 test was used to estimate relative risks (RRs) with 95% CIs. In total, 39 patients with dMMR/MSI-H GC/GEJC who received neoadjuvant immunotherapy were included. All patients underwent complete R0 resection; 22 patients (56%) achieved pCR in both the primary tumor and lymph nodes. The chemotherapy plus immunotherapy group and the immunotherapy-only group achieved significantly higher TRG1 rates compared with the chemotherapy group (RR=4.2, 95% CI=1.5-15.0, P=0.0004; and RR=4.4, 95% CI=1.7-15.7, P=0.003, respectively). The intestinal subtype also demonstrated a higher TRG1 rate than the mixed subtype (RR=2.5, 95% CI=1.1-8.7, P=0.0196). Neoadjuvant immunotherapy achieved a high pCR rate in patients with dMMR/MSI-H locally advanced, resectable GC/GEJC relative to chemotherapy. The intestinal subtype may serve as a histologic biomarker of enhanced sensitivity to neoadjuvant immunotherapy in this patient population.

title: Lactylation-Mediated HER2 Stabilization Promotes Trastuzumab Resistance in Gastric Cancer.
abstract: Trastuzumab is the standard first-line targeted therapy for human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-positive gastric cancer (GC). Unfortunately, its clinical efficacy is often compromised by the development of drug resistance. The Warburg effect, a hallmark of cancer metabolism, leads to substantial lactate accumulation. Nevertheless, the impact of metabolic reprogramming on the response to HER2-targeted therapy remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that AARS1-mediated lactylation of HER2 promotes trastuzumab resistance in GC. Mechanistically, lactylation at lysine 1171 (K1171) promotes USP11-mediated deubiquitination and stabilization of HER2 and also enhances the interaction between HER2 and EGFR. Clinically, elevated HER2 K1171 lactylation levels are associated with poor prognosis in GC patients. Inhibiting HER2 K1171 lactylation with L-alanine or stiripentol-a lactate dehydrogenase inhibitor (LDHi) clinically approved for epilepsy-significantly sensitizes tumor cells to trastuzumab. Furthermore, a cell-penetrating peptide designed to specifically block HER2 K1171 lactylation potently enhances antitumor efficacy in vivo. In summary, our findings identify HER2 lactylation as a critical mechanism underlying trastuzumab resistance and highlight lactate metabolism as a promising therapeutic target for HER2-positive GC.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Low-Dose Hypofractionated Radiotherapy Combined with Immunotherapy for Liver Metastases: A Single-Center Retrospective Analysis.
abstract: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of low-dose hypofractionated radiotherapy (LDHRT) for liver metastases when combined with immunotherapy. Patients with liver metastases receiving immunotherapy were enrolled in this study at Changzhou Second People's Hospital from January 2019 to May 2025 (Ethics Approval No. [2021]KY117-01). LDHRT (12 Gy in 3 fractions) was administered to the liver metastases using volumetric modulated arc therapy (VMAT). The tumor response was evaluated according to the RECIST 1.1 standard. Clinical and imaging data were collected to assess changes in tumors inside and outside the radiation field before and after LDHRT, as well as the median progression-free survival (PFS) for lesions within the radiation field. A total of 51 patients were included, with the median age of 69 (range 47-84) years; 86.3% (44/51) were male, and 94.1% (48/51) had an ECOG performance status (PS) score ≥1. Additionally, 54.9% (28/51) had received ≥3 lines of prior therapy. Due to the continuous progression of liver metastases under systemic treatment, LDHRT was administered for the liver metastases. The study found a high local control rate within the radiation field as the objective response rate (ORR) and disease control rate (DCR) within the radiation field were 17.6% and 86.3%, respectively. However, the efficacy for lesions outside the radiation field was significantly inferior, with an ORR of 0% and a DCR of 35.3%. The median PFS for lesions within the radiation field was 4.23 months. Patients with colorectal liver metastases (CRLM) showed better PFS than those with gastric cancer liver metastases (GCLM). The most common adverse events were fatigue (16/51, 31.4%), abnormal liver function (11/51, 21.6%), and hypothyroidism (7/51, 13.7%). No patients discontinued treatment due to treatment-related adverse events. LDHRT combined with immunotherapy provided favorable local control and was generally well tolerated in patients with liver metastases. No apparent abscopal effect was observed, suggesting that single-lesion LDHRT was insufficient to reverse systemic immunosuppression.

title: A case of recurrent early gastric cancer with a giant injection-related granuloma after endoscopic submucosal dissection resulting in non-curative resection.
abstract: A 69-year-old man underwent endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) for early gastric cancer of the lower gastric body. The lateral margin was positive, corresponding to an eCura C-1 classification, and surveillance with upper gastrointestinal endoscopy every 6 months was performed. Local recurrence was detected 4 years later, and repeat ESD resulted in an eCura C-2 classification, prompting additional surgical resection. No lymph node metastasis was identified, and the patient remained recurrence-free for 11 months. Histopathological examination of the surgical specimen revealed extensive foreign body granuloma formation involving the deep muscularis propria and subserosal tissue. The granulomas were Alcian-blue positive, with staining intensity reduced after hyaluronidase treatment, suggesting the involvement of a hyaluronic acid-containing submucosal injection agent. No granulomas were observed in the repeat ESD specimen obtained 6 months before surgery. Inflammatory cell infiltration around the lymphatic vessels was observed, suggesting the involvement of lymphatic pathways to the gradual spread and extensive distribution of the granulomatous reaction over time. Submucosal injection-related granuloma formation after ESD is rare, but extensive granuloma formation may complicate the interpretation of post-ESD findings and potentially increase the technical difficulty of subsequent treatment. Clinicians should be aware of this possibility when performing surveillance and additional treatment after ESD.

title: Molecular mechanism of Xanthotoxol against gastric cancer: A comprehensive study integrating network pharmacology, computer simulations, and experimental validation.
abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) is a prevalent malignant tumor of the digestive system worldwide. Xanthotoxol (Xan), a natural compound extracted from traditional Chinese medicine such as Angelica archangelica, has demonstrated antitumor properties. However, its specific effects on GC remain unreported. Hub targets of Xan in GC were identified by integrating weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) with network pharmacology. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were conducted to analyze the interaction between the hub targets and Xan. The effects of Xan on GC cell proliferation, cell cycle, apoptosis, migration, and invasion were examined using cell experiments and xenograft tumor model. Histopathological evaluation of changes in tumor and liver tissues was performed after Xan intervention. Western blot and reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) were employed to analyze hub target expression and clarify Xan's molecular mechanism against GC. A total of six hub genes highly correlated with GC were identified (MMP12, KDR, CCND1, PDGFRB, PLAU, and PLK1). Molecular docking and MD simulations revealed a significant binding affinity between Xan and hub genes. Experiments demonstrated that Xan inhibited proliferation, cell cycle, migration, and invasion while promoting apoptosis. Xan could alleviate liver injury caused by subcutaneous tumor in mice. Furthermore, Xan upregulated MMP12 expression and downregulated KDR, CCND1, PDGFRB, PLAU, and PLK1 in GC cells. Xan shows promise as a GC treatment by modulating MMP12, KDR, CCND1, PDGFRB, PLAU, and PLK1 expression, which inhibits proliferation, cell cycle, migration, and invasion, while enhancing apoptosis and reducing liver damage.

title: ASTRUM-006 and the changing landscape of perioperative therapy for gastric cancer.
abstract: ASTRUM-006 provides phase 3 evidence that perioperative immune checkpoint inhibition improves event-free survival with Asian SOX-based chemotherapy in PD-L1-positive gastric cancer. Its postoperative chemotherapy-sparing strategy is attractive, although unmasking, event adjudication, and non-R0 or occult metastatic disease warrant consideration. The study nevertheless broadens the perioperative treatment framework and provides an important platform for refining patient selection and postoperative treatment intensity.

title: The prognostic value of HER2 in gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma - a meta-analysis.
abstract: HER2 amplification and overexpression are predictive markers for HER2-targeted therapies in gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma. However, unlike in breast cancer, the prognostic significance of HER2 status in this disease remains uncertain, with conflicting evidence across studies. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies reporting hazard ratios (HRs) for overall survival (OS) based on HER2 status, identified through PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science. Eligible studies included HER2-positive and HER2-negative patients with gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma, using IHC and/or ISH diagnostics. Pooled HRs were calculated using random-effects models. Subgroup analyses and meta-regressions were performed by stage, treatment, and covariates. A novel statistical framework was applied to contextualize HER2's prognostic role. Eighty studies encompassing 30,574 patients were included. HER2 positivity was associated with poorer OS in univariate analyses for stage I-III (HR 1.29, 95% CI: 1.02-1.61) and stage I-IV disease (HR 1.58, 95% CI: 1.14-2.20), and remained significant in multivariate analyses (HR 1.46 and HR 1.52, respectively). In metastatic disease, HER2 positivity was associated with poorer survival in untreated cohorts (multivariate HR 1.37, 95% CI: 1.01-1.85; p = 0.043), but with improved survival in trastuzumab-treated cohorts in univariate analysis (HR 0.73, 95% CI: 0.61-0.88; p = 0.0007) and borderline multivariate analysis (HR 0.71, 95% CI: 0.50-1.00; p = 0.047). HER2 positivity was independently associated with poorer overall survival in gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma. In metastatic disease, pooled estimates differed according to trastuzumab exposure, with more favorable outcomes observed in trastuzumab-treated HER2-positive cohorts. These findings support an adverse prognostic association of HER2 positivity and further investigation of HER2-directed therapy in earlier-stage disease.

title: Analysis of a case of immune-related pancreatitis induced by anti-PD-1 antibody therapy for gastric cancer: A case report.
abstract: Immune-related pancreatitis is a rare but clinically significant adverse event associated with immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy. Early recognition and appropriate management are essential to prevent potentially serious outcomes. Herein, we report a case of suspected immune-related pancreatitis during nivolumab-based immunotherapy for metastatic gastric cancer. An 82-year-old female patient, post-gastrectomy for gastric cancer with subsequent cerebral metastases, multiple leptomeningeal metastases, subcutaneous metastases, and retroperitoneal lymph node metastases, received "nivolumab + apatinib" therapy for 4 cycles. On the second day of the fourth cycle of treatment, the patient developed mild epigastric pain, acid regurgitation, and elevated pancreatic enzyme levels, suggestive of immune-related pancreatitis. Alternative etiologies, including biliary disease, alcohol use, and hypertriglyceridemia, were excluded. The patient was classified as Grade 1 according to the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events v5.0 and was managed with fasting, parenteral nutrition, octreotide, enzyme inhibition, and electrolyte balance adjustment. Pancreatic enzyme levels normalized, and symptoms resolved. Nivolumab and apatinib were subsequently withheld. This case highlights that immune-related pancreatitis may present with only mild abdominal symptoms despite marked pancreatic enzyme elevation during immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy. Clinicians should maintain a high index of suspicion for pancreatic immune-related adverse events, even in the absence of typical imaging findings, and systematically exclude alternative causes to ensure timely and appropriate management.

title: Gastric cancer burden from 1990 to 2021, Joinpoint analysis, projections to 2036, and health inequality assessment: Findings from the Global Burden of Disease study 2021.
abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) remains a major global health issue with high incidence and mortality. This study evaluates the global burden and health disparities of GC from 1990 to 2021 and projects trends through 2036, providing evidence for targeted control measures. The data were sourced from the 2021 Global Burden of Disease study, covering the incidence, mortality, disability-adjusted life years, age-standardized incidence rate, age-standardized mortality rate, and age-standardized disability-adjusted life years rate of GC across 204 countries and regions from 1990 to 2021. Joinpoint regression analysis was employed to examine trends between 1990 and 2021, while a Bayesian age-period-cohort model was constructed to assess and project trends up to 2036. Concentration curves and concentration indices were used to examine cross-national relative inequalities in GC burden across sociodemographic index (SDI) levels. Compared to 1990, the number of GC cases and deaths increased in 2021; meanwhile, the age-standardized incidence rate, age-standardized mortality rate, and age-standardized disability-adjusted life years rate declined, respectively. Males consistently faced a higher disease burden across all age groups. The gap between high-SDI and low-SDI countries is narrowing, with underdeveloped countries bearing a relatively heavier burden of stomach cancer. The Bayesian age-period-cohort model predicts a further decline in the global GC burden by 2036. GC remains a substantial global burden, affecting regions and countries worldwide with pronounced geographic, age, and sex-related disparities. Effective interventions - such as Helicobacter pylori prevention and treatment, as well as widespread early GC screening - are crucial for reducing incidence risks and improving survival outcomes.

title: Biomaterial-driven remove-remodel-repair (3R) strategy for full-cycle gastric cancer management: bibliometric mapping, preclinical evidence, and a translational roadmap.
abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) remains a leading cause of cancer mortality worldwide and is characterized by prolonged precancerous progression, dynamic tumor-immune-microbiota interactions, and treatment-associated toxicity that can compromise host defense and tissue recovery. These features create a clinical need for full-cycle management spanning prevention, early eradication, advanced therapy, and postoperative rehabilitation. Here, we propose a biomaterial-driven 3R framework for GC management across the disease continuum, comprising remove for lesion clearance, remodel for immune microenvironment regulation, and repair for tissue restoration. A bibliometric analysis of 1559 publications maps the evolution of biomaterial-enabled GC research and provides an evidence landscape for this framework. Representative nanomaterials, biomimetic hydrogels, engineered microbial carriers, and regenerative matrices are mapped to clinical needs across prevention, endoscopic and perioperative intervention, systemic therapy, and rehabilitation. The 3R occupy distinct translational tiers: remove- and remodel-oriented platforms are predominantly supported by mechanistic preclinical studies, whereas selected repair-oriented materials, including endoscopic hemostatic, sealing, and submucosal-support platforms, already have human clinical evidence. Overall, the 3R framework links therapeutic objectives, material functions, disease stages, and clinically relevant endpoints into a translational roadmap for integrated GC management.

title: Indocyanine green-guided lymphadenectomy and survival of patients with gastric cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis of time-to-event data.
abstract: Indocyanine green fluorescence imaging (ICG-FI) is increasingly used for lymph node mapping in gastric cancer (GC) surgery, but its impact on long-term oncologic outcomes remains unclear. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the long-term survival benefits of ICG-guided lymphadenectomy compared with conventional surgery. PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library were searched from inception to November 2025, supplemented by clinical trial registries. Studies comparing ICG-guided versus non-ICG-guided lymphadenectomy in GC patients were included. Primary outcomes were overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS). Secondary outcomes included lymph node yield and postoperative complications. Random-effects models were used, and Bayesian analyses estimated the probability of survival benefit. Seven studies comprising 7518 patients were included. ICG significantly improved 3-year OS (HR = 0.635, 95% CI 0.511-0.790, P = 0.000), 3-year DFS (HR = 0.682, 95% CI 0.530-0.877, P = 0.003), and 5-year OS (HR = 0.700, 95% CI 0.507-0.966, P = 0.030), with Bayesian posterior probabilities of 100%, 100%, and 99.1%, respectively. No significant differences were observed for 2-year OS or DFS. ICG significantly increased lymph node yield (WMD = 6.557, 95% C1 3.821-9.294, P = 0.000) without increasing postoperative complications (RR = 0.899, 95% CI 0.647-1.250, P = 0.527). ICG-guided lymphadenectomy is associated with improved long-term survival and increased lymph node dissection without increasing complications. These findings support ICG-FI as a valuable adjunct in gastric cancer surgery. Further high-quality randomized trials are warranted to validate these results in diverse populations and settings.
